findings.issue_text: [BUG] `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, a Ruby 2.1+ method, but this repository's runtime is Ruby 1.9/2.0 (the Gemfile itself still carries the comment "perftools only works on 1.9 atm", and .ruby-version pins 2.0.0 at this point in history), so the method does not exist. The first time PollFeed runs with feed_polling_enabled, `poll_feed` raises NoMethodError: undefined method `scrub' for String, the job dies (sidekiq_options retry: false), and feed polling silently never imports anything.

[BUG] The code assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes a `content` field, but SimpleRSS returns nil for `content` on feeds that only carry `description`, so `i.content.scrub` is called on nil. Any feed whose items lack a content element makes PollFeed crash with NoMethodError on nil on every hourly run; a single malformed item aborts the whole feed import for that cycle.

[BUG] `params.require(:embed_url)` relies on ActionController::Parameters from Rails 4, but the repository's primary Gemfile.lock is still Rails 3.2 (this PR updates only the parallel Gemfile_rails4.lock), and Rails 3.2's params is a HashWithIndifferentAccess with no #require method. On the Rails 3.2 stack that the main lockfile drives, every request to /embed/best raises NoMethodError: undefined method `require' and renders a 500 instead of either the embed view or the loading page; the controller spec's success-context assertions would also fail on this stack.

[BUG] Only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated to include ruby-readability and simple-rss; the primary Gemfile.lock that the default bundle resolves against is left out of sync with the modified Gemfile. Any environment bundling against the main lockfile (CI, production deploy with bundle --frozen/deployment) fails with 'could not find ruby-readability-0.5.7 in any of the sources' because the lockfile does not contain the gems the Gemfile now requires.

[ADVISORY] The new top-level assets embed.css.scss and embed.js are never registered in the asset precompile list; the diff touches no config/application.rb or initializer, and Rails' default precompile pattern only includes files named application.*. In production, `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` raises "embed.css isn't precompiled" and /assets/embed.js 404s, so every third-party page embedding comments gets a broken iframe even though the feature works in development.

[ADVISORY] The only new logic that is actually tested is the SiteSetting gate; `poll_feed`, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and TopicRetriever's perform_retrieve/fetch_http paths are entirely uncovered — the poll_feed spec stubs poll_feed out and the retriever spec stubs perform_retrieve out. A regression in feed parsing, URL absolutization, or the HTTP fetch path (e.g. the nil-content and scrub crashes above) ships undetected because no test in this diff exercises those code paths.

[BUG] PollFeed assumes every feed item has a `content` element, but RSS 2.0 feeds put the body in `description`, so `i.content` is nil and `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. For any RSS 2.0 feed (the most common format), the hourly job crashes on the first item with NoMethodError; because sidekiq_options retry: false is set, no retry happens and zero topics are ever imported, with no per-item rescue so one malformed item also aborts import of all remaining items every run.

[BUG] The imported-from footer interpolates the raw embed URL into an HTML attribute without escaping: "#{url}", and the only gate is the /^https?\:\/\// prefix check which permits quotes and HTML metacharacters in the rest of the URL. A feed item or retriever URL like http://x/'>

[BUG] The new raw_html cook method makes Post#cook return the raw string unsanitized, and both ingest paths feed untrusted remote HTML into it: PollFeed stores CGI.unescapeHTML(feed content) with no sanitize/readability pass at all, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19). Script or event-handler markup in any item of the configured feed (content fully attacker-controlled if the feed is third-party) is stored as cooked HTML and executes as stored XSS for readers of the topic and of the embedded comments iframe; the normal cooking pipeline whose sanitization this relies on is explicitly skipped.

[BUG] TopicEmbed declares belongs_to :topic/:post with no dependent cleanup, and nothing in the diff removes topic_embeds rows when their topic is deleted, while EmbedController#best (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-11) still looks up topics by the stale topic_id. After a moderator deletes an imported topic, topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id, TopicView.new raises on the missing topic, and the third-party page's embed iframe gets a permanent 500 on every pageview instead of falling back to retrieval or an empty state.

[ADVISORY] Jobs::RetrieveTopic ships with no spec: the diff's test-shaped files are spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, and spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb — none covers this job. The job's user lookup and staff no_throttle branching (the code that decides whether an anonymous embed view can bypass the 60-second retrieval throttle) is uncovered; a regression there either disables embed retrieval entirely or turns the throttle off for anonymous users, and no test in the diff would fail.

[ADVISORY] The poll_feed spec only stubs poll_feed out and tests the three execute() gating flags; the actual import loop (SimpleRSS parsing, i.content/i.link handling, TopicEmbed.import wiring) is never exercised by any test in the diff. A regression in the item-processing loop — e.g. the nil-content crash, wrong URL fallback, or title pass-through — lands on an hourly production job with zero failing tests, and the admin discovers it only by noticing no posts appear.

[ADVISORY] iframe.src is built as discourseUrl + "embed/best?..." which silently requires the embedded discourseUrl to end with a trailing slash, and neither the snippet nor the code validates or normalizes it. A site owner who pastes their forum URL without the trailing slash gets iframe.src like "https://forum.example.comembed/best?...", the iframe 404s forever, and the comments simply never appear with no error message pointing at the misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring matching — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1 — so any origin whose string contains the discourse URL as a prefix passes the gate. A page at an origin like https://example.com.evil.example (with discourseUrl https://example.com) passes the indexOf check and can drive the resize handler; the practical impact is limited to manipulating iframe height on the attacker's own page, but the check does not verify what it appears to verify.

[ADVISORY] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, with no terminal state for the case where retrieval never succeeds. For an embed_url whose article cannot be fetched (404, timeout, non-HTML page), a visitor's browser loops forever: each reload finds no topic and enqueues another RetrieveTopic job (throttled to one per 60 seconds per URL), so the page never shows content or an error and keeps generating background work indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] The three new embedding settings ship with no validation and no feedback path: feed_polling_url accepts any string, and when embed_by_username matches no user both poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28) and TopicRetriever#fetch_http (lib/topic_retriever.rb:50) silently return. An admin who typos the username or feed URL gets a feature that appears configured but imports nothing, hour after hour, with no error in the admin UI or logs surfaced to them; there is no way to discover the misconfiguration except reading code.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls rewrites any a[href]/img[src] starting with '/', which includes protocol-relative URLs ('//cdn.example.com/x'), producing malformed results like "http://site.com//cdn.example.com/x". Articles from feeds that use scheme-relative CDN asset URLs (a common modern convention) get broken image srcs and broken link hrefs in the imported post, visibly corrupting imported content for those sources.

[ADVISORY] The diff modifies an unrelated, already-applied migration (create_top_topics) to add `force: true`, work with no traceability to the embed URL handling intent. Reviewers and bisecters of the embedding feature must wade through unrelated migration churn; if this migration is ever re-run against a database that already has top_topics data (e.g. rebuilt dev/CI databases), force: true silently drops and recreates the table, discarding all rows.

[ADVISORY] The diff touches an unrelated shipped migration with whitespace-only edits (trailing-space removal, EOF newline stripped), work not traceable to any embedding requirement. Noise pollutes the diff and risks accidental merge conflicts on a migration that is frozen history; anyone auditing this PR for embedding behavior must verify these lines do nothing, which costs review time on every pass.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently removes the public `--category`/`-c` CLI option and its category_id wiring from disqus:import, repurposing the importer to fetch remote article content via TopicEmbed.import_remote instead. Existing automation invoking `thor disqus:import -c "Some Category"` no longer assigns any category — imported topics land in the site default with no error and no migration path; a functional removal is buried inside a PR whose stated scope is embed URL handling and validation.

[ADVISORY] The diff bundles an entire RSS/Atom feed-polling subsystem (hourly scheduled job, three new site settings, simple-rss gem dependency, and a synchronous RSS branch inside TopicRetriever) that is not traceable to the stated embed URL handling and validation intent. Every deployment of this PR gains a permanently scheduled hourly job that fetches and parses an external URL and creates/updates topics, even for sites that only wanted iframe embedding; the feature cannot be evaluated or reverted independently of the embed-comment feature it rides in with.

[BUG] `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (nil), and `sidekiq_options retry: false` ensures the run is not retried. Any feed containing a single summary-only or content-less item (common for Atom feeds with only <summary>) makes every hourly poll die at that item, so all articles after it are never imported and the feature fails silently with no retry and no error surfaced to the operator.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside the user-triggered retrieval path, coupling the interactive embed request to a full external feed fetch with no timeout (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`). A visitor hitting embed/best for an unknown URL causes a Sidekiq worker to fetch and parse the entire configured feed synchronously; a slow or hanging feed server blocks the worker indefinitely, and the coupling means enabling feed_polling changes the latency and failure profile of the embed-comment path even for URLs the feed will never contain.

[ADVISORY] The new non-trivial logic in TopicEmbed.import_remote, absolutize_urls (port handling, path collapsing), and PollFeed#poll_feed's parsing/URL-fallback body has no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in remote HTML extraction or relative-URL absolutization (e.g. ports being dropped or duplicated slashes on nonstandard ports) would ship undetected and corrupt every imported article's links and images; only the import happy path and job gating are exercised by topic_embed_spec.rb and poll_feed_spec.rb.

[BUG] PollFeed calls `i.content.scrub`, but plain RSS 2.0 feeds expose the body as `description`, not `content`, so `i.content` is nil/undefined and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The hourly poll job crashes on the first item of any RSS 2.0 feed that uses <description> instead of <content:encoded>; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the crash is swallowed and feed polling is silently and permanently dead — no topics are ever created and no error is surfaced to the operator.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import uses check-then-insert (SELECT on embed_url at line 15, then TopicEmbed.create! at line 25 inside the transaction) with no lock, while both the PollFeed job and TopicRetriever jobs can import the same URL concurrently. Two concurrent imports of the same URL both see `embed.blank?`, both create a topic/post, and the loser's TopicEmbed.create! raises on the unique embed_url index; inside Jobs::PollFeed (retry: false) that exception aborts the entire hourly run, so every remaining feed item after the duplicated one is skipped for that cycle.

[ADVISORY] `feed_key` ("feed-modified:..." Redis key) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff — the conditional-get/modified check it was built for was never wired in. Dead code that misleads maintainers into thinking modified-only polling exists; every hour the job fetches and re-parses the full feed and runs a SELECT + import decision per item regardless of whether anything changed, and the next person changing polling logic has to discover the key is phantom.

[ADVISORY] The throttle uses `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` — the two-step SETNX+EXPIRE race — instead of an atomic SET with EX/NX. If the process dies (or Redis connection drops) between the SETNX and the EXPIRE, the key persists with no TTL and that embed_url is throttled forever: the article can never be imported again for any non-staff visitor, permanently showing the loading state.

[ADVISORY] The update path in import only revises the post body; the `title` argument is accepted but never written, so a changed article title never propagates to the existing topic. An editor who retitles an article on their blog gets a topic whose body updates every poll but whose title stays the original headline forever, with no way to reconcile short of deleting the embed row — the topic title and source article silently diverge.

[ADVISORY] Both external fetches (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` here and `open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout. A stalled or slow-loris feed/article server hangs the sidekiq thread indefinitely (open-uri has no default open timeout); with retry: false the hourly poll slot is consumed by the hung thread and repeated hangs exhaust the sidekiq worker pool, stalling unrelated background jobs on the instance.

[ADVISORY] Every request for a not-yet-imported embed_url unconditionally enqueues a retrieve_topic job; the dedup/throttle (redis setnx) lives inside the job, not at enqueue time. A popular article that fails or delays import (e.g., embed_by_username unset, host mismatch, upstream down) gets one sidekiq job enqueued per page view per visitor; the queue floods with no-op jobs that each only discover the throttle after dequeue, starving the job queue for the duration of the traffic spike.

[ADVISORY] Article identity is raw string equality on `embed_url` (exact-match WHERE plus a unique index on the un-normalized string column), with no canonicalization of scheme, trailing slash, query params, or case. The same article discovered via two paths — the feed's `i.link` from PollFeed and the page URL the embedding site passes to /embed/best — is two different strings, creating two topics for one article (the unique index cannot dedupe them), and the iframe on the article page shows the discussion from whichever variant happened to match.

[ADVISORY] The `raw_html` cook_method short-circuits `cook` by returning `raw` unmodified, which changes the contract of `Post#cooked` from 'sanitized rendered HTML' to 'whatever bytes were stored' for an entire class of posts. Every consumer of #cooked outside this diff's embed view — notification emails, search indexing, excerpts, serializations to clients — now receives raw externally-sourced HTML for imported posts; each existing caller inherits unparsed markup (e.g., tags visible in emails/search text) and the next feature that trusts `cooked` being sanitized silently breaks for these rows.

[ADVISORY] topic_embeds carries both topic_id and post_id (post_id derivable from the topic) with no FK, no dependent-destroy wiring, and no cleanup path anywhere in the diff when the topic or its first post is deleted. Deleting an embedded topic (a normal user/moderator action) leaves the row behind; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id, so every embed iframe for that article renders a TopicView on a deleted topic — an error page or eternal loading loop instead of a clean state.

[ADVISORY] The loading view blindly reloads every 30 seconds with no terminal state and no error signal from the retrieve path (which fails silently by design: user missing, host invalid, fetch error, non-URL all produce no topic). When import fails for any reason, the third-party article page shows 'Loading Discussion...' reloading forever, burning bandwidth on both the embedding site and the forum with no diagnostics distinguishing 'in progress' from 'permanently broken'.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus import silently changed its contract: the `--category` option was removed, and topic creation moved from building a post from the Disqus data to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which live-fetches each thread's `t[:link]` over HTTP at import time. Existing invocations using `-c` now fail with an unknown-option error, and archiving an old forum whose article links are dead or redirect-walled makes import_remote return nil per thread so every thread and its replies are silently skipped with no report of what was dropped.

[BUG] The artifact does not implement the stated objective 'Enhance embed URL handling and validation' — it silently introduces an entire new embedding/RSS-import feature (new gems, EmbedController, TopicEmbed model, two schema migrations, PollFeed/RetrieveTopic jobs, four new site settings) whose scope was never stated in, nor accepted against, the original objective. Review iterations drifted the deliverable from 'URL handling and validation' to a full feed-importing subsystem including new third-party dependencies (ruby-readability, simple-rss), a new posts.cook_method column, and a new topic_embeds table; a future maintainer auditing the accepted constraints cannot map any of these schema and dependency changes to an accepted requirement, and any rejection of the feature as-scoped arrives after schema and core-model changes have already landed.

[BUG] The cook_method :raw_html branch makes Post#cook return the raw attribute directly, so externally-supplied RSS content imported by TopicEmbed.import bypasses the entire sanitization/cooking pipeline and is emitted unescaped via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:22 — the opposite of the 'validation' behavior the PR title claims to enhance. An attacker who controls (or can inject an item into) the configured feed_polling_url publishes script or event-handler HTML in an RSS item; TopicEmbed.import stores it verbatim (skip_validations: true in both create and revise paths), and any visitor of the embed page executes it as stored XSS in the forum's origin.

[BUG] The diff silently removes the public `--category/-c` CLI option and replaces the permalink-post creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote, changing what the existing disqus import command accepts and produces without any mention in the PR's stated objective. Existing operator scripts invoking `thor disqus import -c 'Some Category'` now abort with a Thor unknown-switch error, and even corrected invocations no longer create the '[Permalink](url)' post with category assignment — instead they fetch each Disqus thread's live URL over HTTP and import the scraped article, silently changing the imported data shape for every existing user of the task.

[ADVISORY] An already-shipped, unrelated migration (CreateTopTopics) is silently modified to add `force: true`, a change with no connection to the embed objective and no record of human acceptance. Anyone running db:migrate:redo (or re-running the migration against an environment where top_topics already holds computed ranking data) silently drops and recreates the table, destroying the data; the edit also buries an unrelated behavioral change inside a feature PR, so future archaeology of the migration history misattributes its purpose.

[ADVISORY] The already-applied MigrateWordCounts migration is reformatted (trailing whitespace stripped, final newline removed) as a no-functionality change bundled into the embed PR. The next change-safety loss is attribution: a functional edit to this migration later will be mixed with this cosmetic churn, and any diff-based audit of migration files now shows drift against the deployed version with no corresponding intent, making it harder to verify that production databases match the repository's migration lineage.

[ADVISORY] The core revision path is changed from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, introducing a permanent validation-bypass lever into PostRevisor solely to serve the embed importer, with no explicit acceptance of that weakening of the shared validation system. Every future caller that passes skip_validations: true silently writes posts that skip all validations (length, banned words, topic state), and because the flag lives in a shared opts hash rather than a scoped importer path, the next feature that needs to 'skip one check' will reach for it, eroding validation guarantees invisibly — directly contradicting the PR's stated 'validation' objective.

[BUG] The new :raw_html cook_method returns the post's raw content verbatim (return raw), completely bypassing the sanitize/cooking pipeline, and TopicEmbed.import feeds third-party RSS/Atom content into posts with cook_method: raw_html, so untrusted HTML (script tags, event handlers, javascript: URLs) is stored and rendered unsanitized. Stored XSS on the Discourse origin: an attacker who controls feed content (any co-author on the configured feed, or a man-in-the-middle since PollFeed fetches over plain HTTP with open()) publishes an item whose content contains or

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the raw URL into an HTML fragment with single-quoted attributes ("#{url}") and appends it to content that is then stored as raw HTML, without any escaping of the URL. A feed item (or embed URL) like http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover='alert(document.cookie) passes the /^https?\:\/\// check, breaks out of the href attribute, and is stored in the post; because cook_method is raw_html the payload is served verbatim to every reader of the topic and the embed view, yielding stored XSS.

[BUG] PollFeed passes the admin-settable SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly into Kernel#open with no scheme validation, so file://, ftp://, or internal-network http URLs are fetched server-side and their contents are imported into public topics. An admin account compromise (or a site_settings write via any admin-reachable path) setting feed_polling_url to file:///etc/passwd or http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data causes local file or internal service contents to be parsed as a feed and published as posts readable by all users — server-side file disclosure / SSRF with no protocol allowlist.

[BUG] The postMessage origin check uses a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of equality, so any origin whose string contains discourseUrl as a substring is accepted as a trusted sender. An attacker page hosted at e.g. https://forum.example.com.attacker.com (or attacker.com?x=https://forum.example.com-style substrings) passes the check and can postMessage {type:'discourse-resize', height:...} to resize the embedded comments iframe arbitrarily (UI defacement / clickjacking-layout manipulation inside the embedding page).

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL", which is not a valid X-Frame-Options value; browsers that do not recognize it ignore the header entirely, so this response's framing protection depends entirely on the referer check. Any future code path that relaxes or removes the referer check (or a browser/configuration that drops Referer) leaves the embed endpoint frameable by every origin with no XFO backstop; the value should be an allow-from mechanism or header deletion, not a non-standard token.

[ADVISORY] The controller enqueues a retrieve_topic Sidekiq job for every request that misses the topic lookup, with no rate limit at the enqueue site; the 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever.retrieved_recently? keyed per-URL, so distinct URL paths each get a fresh throttle budget and the enqueue itself is unthrottled and unauthenticated. An unauthenticated client spamming /embed/best?embed_url=http://<embeddable_host>/<random> floods the Sidekiq queue with jobs (each job performs a Redis SETNX plus potentially an outbound HTTP fetch), exhausting background-job capacity; the per-URL Redis key provides no defense because the attacker varies the path.

[ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url).read before any scheme/host validation — TopicEmbed.import's /^https?\:\/\// check runs only after the fetch — so callers that bypass TopicRetriever's host check fetch unvalidated URLs; the disqus.thor import path passes t[:link] straight from an attacker-supplied Disqus export XML into import_remote. An admin who imports a crafted Disqus export file causes the server to open file:// or internal-network URLs listed in it, with the fetched bytes rendered into public posts — a config/import-backed SSRF/LFI path distinct from the (host-checked) TopicRetriever path.

[BUG] The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" never exercises the params.require(:embed_url) branch it claims to verify: with the default blank embeddable_host (config/site_settings.yml line 354: embeddable_host: ''), the ensure_embeddable before_filter raises Discourse::InvalidAccess before the controller action body runs, so get :best fails at the filter, not at the missing param. The missing-embed_url branch is asserted by nothing: if params.require(:embed_url) were deleted entirely (or if the filter order changed so the param check surfaced as a 500 instead of the promised 404), this test still passes because 'response.should_not be_success' is true for any error status — the spec name and the behavior it verifies are unrelated, giving false confidence that the embed_url contract is tested.

[ADVISORY] The only test that runs with the gating satisfied stubs poll_feed itself ('poller.expects(:poll_feed).once'), so the entire body of Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (SimpleRSS parsing, the url = i.id fallback for links not matching /^https?/, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and the TopicEmbed.import call) is never executed by any test in this diff. A regression in poll_feed — e.g. a feed item whose link is blank and whose item has no id attribute raising NoMethodError, or content mangled before import — ships green; the spec file exists but only verifies that the three SiteSetting guards short-circuit execute, so operators get silent feed-import failures with a passing suite.

[ADVISORY] Both 'valid host' tests stub retrieved_recently? directly ('topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false)' / '.returns(true)'), so the redis throttle logic introduced in this diff ($redis.setnx on 'retrieved:<url>' plus $redis.expire(key, 60), lines 20-29 of lib/topic_retriever.rb) is never executed by any test. The real throttle code is only covered by mocks of itself: a regression where setnx succeeds but expire is never called (leaving a permanent key that throttles the URL forever after the first retrieval), or where the no_throttle branch (user.try(:staff?) from Jobs::RetrieveTopic) is inverted, passes the suite; only the one-line short-circuit 'perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)' is actually verified.

[ADVISORY] The test "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" verifies only that the TopicView mock was constructed with specific args ('TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})') and never asserts anything about the rendered response body; the template then renders against a Mocha mock whose @topic_view.posts.present?, posts.each, and topic.url calls all return truthy mocks, so the 'success' assertion in the after block is satisfied by mock-driven garbage rendering. The test cannot distinguish a correctly rendered embed page from one that renders nothing meaningful: any regression in how @topic_view is consumed by app/views/embed/best.html.erb (e.g. best: 5 being ignored, posts not being passed through) passes as long as the constructor happens to be invoked with those arguments — the assertion verifies the mock call, not the behavior the test name promises.

[ADVISORY] The update test asserts only 'post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/' and never asserts that embed.content_sha1 was updated to the new digest — the very field whose comparison gates the update branch in TopicEmbed.import (lines 30-34). If the update branch stops persisting the new digest (e.g. the 'embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)' line is dropped or writes the stale value), this test still passes because cooked matches the new content, while every subsequent feed poll re-enters the revise branch for the same content indefinitely — the test verifies the symptom (cooked text) but not the mechanism (digest persistence) it exists to cover.

[ADVISORY] The absolutize_urls coverage uses only 'http://eviltrout.com/123' (default port 80), so the non-default-port branch 'prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443' (topic_embed.rb lines 59-60) and the https path are never exercised by any assertion in the diff. A regression on that branch — e.g. unconditionally appending the port, or appending :443 to https URLs — passes the existing assertion, producing rewritten image/link srcs pointing at http://example.com:443/... in imported posts that no test catches.

[BUG] The migration defaults posts.cook_method to 1, which is :raw_html in Post.cook_methods (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns regular=0, raw_html=1), so every existing post and every newly created post without an explicit cook_method is silently reclassified as raw HTML. Post#cook returns `raw` whenever cook_method == raw_html (app/models/post.rb:131-133), so after this migration every pre-existing post renders its uncooked markdown source as its cooked HTML, and all new posts created via the normal PostCreator path (which never sets cook_method) inherit the DB default of 1 and are likewise rendered raw. The author's own spec (topic_embed_spec.rb) proves the value mapping: posts created with cook_method raw_html assert `post.cooked.should == post.raw`. This is a silent reclassification of the entire posts table on deploy; the correct default for the new column is 0 (:regular).

[BUG] This diff adds `force: true` to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making it destructive if it is ever re-run (db:migrate:redo, a restored/mis-recorded schema_migrations row, or an environment replaying the version). Any re-execution of this migration silently drops the existing top_topics table and all of its rows before recreating it empty, destroying the per-topic ranking data until the recalculation job rebuilds it; on a shipped migration this is pure risk with no benefit, since the table already exists in every deployed database. The force: true should be reverted on this already-applied migration.

[ADVISORY] topic_embeds stores topic_id and post_id with null: false but no foreign keys and the diff adds no cleanup hook for deleting the referenced topic or post, so rows are orphaned when a topic is destroyed. When a topic created by embedding is deleted (a normal moderator action), its topic_embeds row survives; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed then keeps returning the dead topic_id, so the embed widget resolves an embed for every page load and EmbedController builds a TopicView against a nonexistent topic instead of falling through to the retrieve/re-create path. A dependent cleanup (or an explicit delete in the topic-destruction path) is needed to keep the mapping table consistent.

[BUG] import_remote calls open(url).read with no explicit open/read timeout and no size cap, buffering the entire remote document in memory. An article served by a slow or broken host wedges the Sidekiq worker for the whole TCP/HTTP timeout window per attempt, and a large or deliberately endless response is read fully into memory; the embed page the user came from just keeps showing the loading screen with no error.

[BUG] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout and no cap on the downloaded feed size. A feed host that hangs or serves a huge body stalls the hourly scheduled job slot; with sidekiq_options retry: false the cycle simply does not run again until the next hour, during which no feed importing happens at all.

[BUG] The rss.items.each loop has no per-item error isolation: an item lacking a `content` tag (e.g. RSS feeds with only <description>), lacking `id` when `link` is unusable, or whose link passes the /^https?\:\/\// regex but fails URI parsing in absolutize_urls raises and aborts the whole loop. One malformed feed item permanently halts import of every item after it: items before the failure are imported, the rest are silently skipped, and with retry: false nothing re-attempts until the next hourly run — the feed silently stops importing new posts while the job still 'ran'.

[BUG] The 60-second throttle key is written to redis (setnx + expire) inside retrieved_recently? before perform_retrieve runs, so the key is committed before the retrieval operation has succeeded. When perform_retrieve raises (network error, 404, readability failure), the key persists for 60 seconds so every subsequent retry job executes retrieve, hits retrieved_recently? and returns silently — retries no-op 'successfully' while no topic is created, and the failure is never surfaced to anyone.

[BUG] The loading page blindly reloads every 30 seconds with no failure state and no termination, while nothing in the retrieval pipeline ever records or reports that retrieval failed. If retrieval permanently fails (article 404s, host serves garbage, import raises), the embedding site's visitors see 'Loading Discussion...' refreshing forever with no error and no fallback link; the user-facing failure is completely invisible.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is dead code — nothing in this diff ever reads or writes the 'feed-modified:...' key it describes. Maintainers are misled into believing modified-since tracking exists; in reality the entire feed is re-fetched and every item re-hashed and re-compared hourly. Deleting the method (or implementing the conditional fetch it implies) removes the false impression.

[ADVISORY] A retrieve_topic job is enqueued on every /embed/best request while the topic is missing, and the 60-second throttle is enforced only inside the job, not at enqueue time. Combined with the loading page's 30-second self-reload, a persistently failing retrieval generates a new Sidekiq job every 30 seconds per open embed indefinitely — unbounded queue growth with each job no-oping against the redis throttle.

[ADVISORY] The update branch ignores revisor.revise!'s return value and unconditionally advances embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) even when the revision did not persist. If revise! returns false or its internal save fails without raising, the new sha1 is stored while the post content was never updated, so all future polls see a matching sha1 and the feed's changed content is permanently never applied — a lost update that looks successful.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import silently returns nil when post creation fails (post.blank? leaves no TopicEmbed and returns nil), and poll_feed discards the return value with no log and no error result. A feed item whose topic/post creation fails is dropped without a trace while the poll job completes 'successfully' — operators have no way to discover that imported articles are missing.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) — a full remote feed fetch and import of every item — inline within the retrieve job whenever feed_polling_enabled? is set. A user's first embed view can block a Sidekiq worker on a complete, timeout-less feed download plus N import operations, compounding the missing-timeout exposure on the request-triggered path; a slow feed host delays every embed retrieval while polling is enabled.
