adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `--category`/`-c` Thor option and all `category_id` lookup/wiring in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (the `method_option :category` line and the `category_id` block are deleted, and the import path is switched to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). That is a concrete, backward-incompatible CLI/API change that should be called out or handled explicitly. However, the finding’s claim that existing automation will “silently” stop assigning a category with “no error” is not verifiable from the diff; Thor may error on unknown switches when `-c` is passed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff bundles an entire RSS/Atom feed-polling subsystem (hourly scheduled job, three new site settings, simple-rss gem dependency, and a synchronous RSS branch inside TopicRetriever) that is not traceable to the stated embed URL handling and validation intent. Every deployment of this PR gains a permanently scheduled hourly job that fetches and parses an external URL and creates/updates topics, even for sites that only wanted iframe embedding; the feature cannot be evaluated or reverted independently of the embed-comment feature it rides in with.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does bundle a substantial feed-import feature set alongside iframe embedding: new gems (`simple-rss`, `ruby-readability`), new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` with `recurrence { hourly }`, new site settings under `embedding:` (`feed_polling_enabled`, `feed_polling_url`, `embed_by_username`), and a synchronous branch in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` that runs the poller when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. However, the finding overstates impact: the hourly job’s `execute` method only calls `poll_feed` when `feed_polling_enabled?` and required settings are present, so it does not “fetch and parse an external URL” on every deployment by default. The core concern (feature coupling/PR scope and inability to evaluate/revert independently) is still real and grounded in the diff, but it’s not a directly verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (nil), and `sidekiq_options retry: false` ensures the run is not retried. Any feed containing a single summary-only or content-less item (common for Atom feeds with only <summary>) makes every hourly poll die at that item, so all articles after it are never imported and the feature fails silently with no retry and no error surfaced to the operator.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is non-nil. If a feed item lacks a `<content>` element (common in Atom feeds that only provide `<summary>`), `i.content` will be `nil` and calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-`rss.items.each`. Because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, it will not retry after such a failure, so subsequent items in the feed won't be imported until the next run and the same item can keep breaking imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside the user-triggered retrieval path, coupling the interactive embed request to a full external feed fetch with no timeout (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`). A visitor hitting embed/best for an unknown URL causes a Sidekiq worker to fetch and parse the entire configured feed synchronously; a slow or hanging feed server blocks the worker indefinitely, and the coupling means enabling feed_polling changes the latency and failure profile of the embed-comment path even for URLs the feed will never contain.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (new file `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`) performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no explicit timeouts/limits, which can block a Sidekiq worker thread during an embed retrieval. This directly changes the latency/failure profile of the retrieval path based on feed polling settings and can hang the worker on slow/hanging feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new non-trivial logic in TopicEmbed.import_remote, absolutize_urls (port handling, path collapsing), and PollFeed#poll_feed's parsing/URL-fallback body has no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in remote HTML extraction or relative-URL absolutization (e.g. ports being dropped or duplicated slashes on nonstandard ports) would ship undetected and corrupt every imported article's links and images; only the import happy path and job gating are exercised by topic_embed_spec.rb and poll_feed_spec.rb.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior that is largely untested: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches remote HTML via `open(url).read` and runs `Readability::Document` (no spec hits this path), `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` builds `prefix` including nonstandard ports and strips leading slashes (`sub(/^\/+/, '')`), but `topic_embed_spec.rb` only asserts absolutization for a simple host with no port and no edge cases. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` contains parsing and URL fallback logic (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, plus `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), while `poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests gating and delegation, not parsing/import behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-coverage gap rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] PollFeed calls `i.content.scrub`, but plain RSS 2.0 feeds expose the body as `description`, not `content`, so `i.content` is nil/undefined and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The hourly poll job crashes on the first item of any RSS 2.0 feed that uses <description> instead of <content:encoded>; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the crash is swallowed and feed polling is silently and permanently dead — no topics are ever created and no error is surfaced to the operator.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `SimpleRSS` items for some feeds do not provide `content` (e.g., only `description`), then `i.content` would be `nil` and calling `.scrub` would raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-run. The diff shows no nil-guard or fallback (like `i.description`), so the job is brittle and can crash on valid feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import uses check-then-insert (SELECT on embed_url at line 15, then TopicEmbed.create! at line 25 inside the transaction) with no lock, while both the PollFeed job and TopicRetriever jobs can import the same URL concurrently. Two concurrent imports of the same URL both see `embed.blank?`, both create a topic/post, and the loser's TopicEmbed.create! raises on the unique embed_url index; inside Jobs::PollFeed (retry: false) that exception aborts the entire hourly run, so every remaining feed item after the duplicated one is skipped for that cycle.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-locked existence check (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and then, if blank, creates a topic/post and finally `TopicEmbed.create!` with the same `embed_url` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent imports of the same URL can both see `embed.blank?`, both create topics/posts, and one will raise on the unique index at `create!`. `Jobs::PollFeed` has `sidekiq_options retry: false` and calls `TopicEmbed.import` in a loop with no rescue, so one such exception would abort the job and skip remaining feed items for that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `feed_key` ("feed-modified:..." Redis key) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff — the conditional-get/modified check it was built for was never wired in. Dead code that misleads maintainers into thinking modified-only polling exists; every hour the job fetches and re-parses the full feed and runs a SELECT + import decision per item regardless of whether anything changed, and the next person changing polling logic has to discover the key is phantom.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `def feed_key` constructs a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but that method is never called anywhere in the diff (not in `execute`, not in `poll_feed`, and not elsewhere). The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on every run and iterates `rss.items` without any conditional-get/If-Modified-Since or Redis-stored modified/etag check. This is dead/unused code that implies an optimization/feature (modified-only polling) that is not actually implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The throttle uses `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` — the two-step SETNX+EXPIRE race — instead of an atomic SET with EX/NX. If the process dies (or Redis connection drops) between the SETNX and the EXPIRE, the key persists with no TTL and that embed_url is throttled forever: the article can never be imported again for any non-staff visitor, permanently showing the loading state.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` the throttling logic in `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This two-step pattern is not atomic; if the process/connection fails after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL. After that, `setnx` will always fail and `retrieved_recently?` will always return `true` for that `embed_url`, permanently preventing `perform_retrieve` for non-throttled users. This is a real behavior implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update path in import only revises the post body; the `title` argument is accepted but never written, so a changed article title never propagates to the existing topic. An editor who retitles an article on their blog gets a topic whose body updates every poll but whose title stays the original headline forever, with no way to reconcile short of deleting the embed row — the topic title and source article silently diverge.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `title` parameter is used only on initial creation (`PostCreator.new(... title: title, ...)`). In the update path (`else` branch), it only revises the post raw via `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, absolutize_urls(...))` and updates `content_sha1`, with no attempt to update the associated topic/post title. Therefore, if the source title changes, subsequent imports/polls cannot propagate that change, and a title-only change wouldn’t even trigger an update since the SHA1 is computed from `contents` only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both external fetches (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` here and `open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout. A stalled or slow-loris feed/article server hangs the sidekiq thread indefinitely (open-uri has no default open timeout); with retry: false the hourly poll slot is consumed by the hung thread and repeated hangs exhaust the sidekiq worker pool, stalling unrelated background jobs on the instance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two external HTTP fetches via open-uri: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Neither call passes explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` (or any other limiting options) or wraps the fetch in error handling, so a slow/stalled remote server can tie up a Sidekiq worker thread for an extended period. The finding’s broader claim about “indefinitely” depends on Ruby/open-uri defaults not shown in the diff, but the lack of explicit timeouts is a real, diff-grounded robustness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every request for a not-yet-imported embed_url unconditionally enqueues a retrieve_topic job; the dedup/throttle (redis setnx) lives inside the job, not at enqueue time. A popular article that fails or delays import (e.g., embed_by_username unset, host mismatch, upstream down) gets one sidekiq job enqueued per page view per visitor; the queue floods with no-op jobs that each only discover the throttle after dequeue, starving the job queue for the duration of the traffic spike.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it always calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb) on every request, with no enqueue-time dedup/throttle. The only throttle is in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? using Redis `setnx` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), which runs when the job is executed (via Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute). If import cannot complete (e.g., TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early when `embed_by_username` user is blank, or host mismatch/invalid URL), topic_id stays nil and subsequent page views keep enqueueing more jobs, potentially flooding Sidekiq with no-op jobs and starving other work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Article identity is raw string equality on `embed_url` (exact-match WHERE plus a unique index on the un-normalized string column), with no canonicalization of scheme, trailing slash, query params, or case. The same article discovered via two paths — the feed's `i.link` from PollFeed and the page URL the embedding site passes to /embed/best — is two different strings, creating two topics for one article (the unique index cannot dedupe them), and the iframe on the article page shows the discussion from whichever variant happened to match.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicEmbed` identifies an article purely by exact string match on `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import`, `topic_id_for_embed` does the same) and the DB enforces uniqueness via `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true` on the raw string. There is no URL normalization/canonicalization (scheme/host case, trailing slash, query params, fragments, etc.) before storing or looking up. Therefore two different URL strings that refer to the same article (e.g., feed `i.link` vs. the page-provided `embed_url` param used by `EmbedController#best`) will create separate `topic_embeds` rows and thus separate topics, and lookup for embedding will only match the exact variant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `raw_html` cook_method short-circuits `cook` by returning `raw` unmodified, which changes the contract of `Post#cooked` from 'sanitized rendered HTML' to 'whatever bytes were stored' for an entire class of posts. Every consumer of #cooked outside this diff's embed view — notification emails, search indexing, excerpts, serializations to clients — now receives raw externally-sourced HTML for imported posts; each existing caller inherits unparsed markup (e.g., tags visible in emails/search text) and the next feature that trusts `cooked` being sanitized silently breaks for these rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline for those posts. `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed` feed/import externally sourced HTML (`doc.content` from `ruby-readability`, and `i.content` from RSS) into `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, so the resulting `post.cooked` becomes whatever raw HTML was stored, without any sanitization/processing shown in this diff. That is a real behavioral change for `#cooked` for imported posts and can leak raw/unsafe markup into any place that uses `post.cooked` (the new embed view even does `raw post.cooked`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_embeds carries both topic_id and post_id (post_id derivable from the topic) with no FK, no dependent-destroy wiring, and no cleanup path anywhere in the diff when the topic or its first post is deleted. Deleting an embedded topic (a normal user/moderator action) leaves the row behind; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id, so every embed iframe for that article renders a TopicView on a deleted topic — an error page or eternal loading loop instead of a clean state.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicEmbed` rows are created with both `topic_id` and `post_id` (migration `create_topic_embeds`) but there are no foreign keys, no `dependent: :destroy` hooks, and no cleanup logic added anywhere. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` blindly returns `pluck(:topic_id).first` for a given `embed_url` without checking that the topic still exists, and `EmbedController#best` then calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` if a `topic_id` is returned. If the associated topic/post is deleted, the `topic_embeds` row can remain and continue returning a now-dead `topic_id`, producing broken embed behavior (error or repeated loading). This is a concrete integrity/behavior defect grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view blindly reloads every 30 seconds with no terminal state and no error signal from the retrieve path (which fails silently by design: user missing, host invalid, fetch error, non-URL all produce no topic). When import fails for any reason, the third-party article page shows 'Loading Discussion...' reloading forever, burning bandwidth on both the embedding site and the forum with no diagnostics distinguishing 'in progress' from 'permanently broken'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an infinite reload loop in the embed iframe when no topic is ever created. `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads every 30s. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always renders `loading` and enqueues `:retrieve_topic`. If retrieval never produces a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#retrieve` returns early on invalid host or malformed URL; `fetch_http` returns if `embed_by_username` user is missing; RSS polling may not create the specific URL), the controller will keep returning `loading` forever with no alternate state or error view, causing repeated requests/bandwidth usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Disqus import silently changed its contract: the `--category` option was removed, and topic creation moved from building a post from the Disqus data to TopicEmbed.import_remote, which live-fetches each thread's `t[:link]` over HTTP at import time. Existing invocations using `-c` now fail with an unknown-option error, and archiving an old forum whose article links are dead or redirect-walled makes import_remote return nil per thread so every thread and its replies are silently skipped with no report of what was dropped.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` the `--category`/`-c` option and all category handling were removed (`method_option :category` and `category_id` lookup deleted). Existing invocations using `-c` will now error as an unknown option. Also, thread creation was changed from a local `PostCreator` call to `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which performs an HTTP fetch (`open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). The importer only processes replies when `post.present?`, with no explicit reporting path when it is nil, so failures to create the topic cause that thread’s replies to be skipped silently apart from the initial "Creating ..." log line.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The artifact does not implement the stated objective 'Enhance embed URL handling and validation' — it silently introduces an entire new embedding/RSS-import feature (new gems, EmbedController, TopicEmbed model, two schema migrations, PollFeed/RetrieveTopic jobs, four new site settings) whose scope was never stated in, nor accepted against, the original objective. Review iterations drifted the deliverable from 'URL handling and validation' to a full feed-importing subsystem including new third-party dependencies (ruby-readability, simple-rss), a new posts.cook_method column, and a new topic_embeds table; a future maintainer auditing the accepted constraints cannot map any of these schema and dependency changes to an accepted requirement, and any rejection of the feature as-scoped arrives after schema and core-model changes have already landed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a full embedding/feed-import feature (new gems, EmbedController, TopicEmbed, jobs, migrations, settings), but the finding’s core claim is that this work contradicts an *unstated* PR objective (“Enhance embed URL handling and validation”) and was “never stated in, nor accepted against” the original scope. That mismatch-to-objective/acceptance context is not present in the diff, so it can’t be verified solely from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cook_method :raw_html branch makes Post#cook return the raw attribute directly, so externally-supplied RSS content imported by TopicEmbed.import bypasses the entire sanitization/cooking pipeline and is emitted unescaped via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:22 — the opposite of the 'validation' behavior the PR title claims to enhance. An attacker who controls (or can inject an item into) the configured feed_polling_url publishes script or event-handler HTML in an RSS item; TopicEmbed.import stores it verbatim (skip_validations: true in both create and revise paths), and any visitor of the embed page executes it as stored XSS in the forum's origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from externally-supplied feed/article HTML using `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` and updates via `PostRevisor#revise!` with `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The embed view then renders it unescaped with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Feed polling only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) which does not sanitize HTML/attributes. Therefore attacker-controlled HTML from `feed_polling_url` (or even via a crafted `url` containing a quote injected into the appended `<a href='#{url}'>` snippet) can be stored and executed as XSS on the Discourse origin when viewing the embed page. This is a real security defect exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff silently removes the public `--category/-c` CLI option and replaces the permalink-post creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote, changing what the existing disqus import command accepts and produces without any mention in the PR's stated objective. Existing operator scripts invoking `thor disqus import -c 'Some Category'` now abort with a Thor unknown-switch error, and even corrected invocations no longer create the '[Permalink](url)' post with category assignment — instead they fetch each Disqus thread's live URL over HTTP and import the scraped article, silently changing the imported data shape for every existing user of the task.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor CLI option `:category` / `-c` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (deleted `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and all `options[:category]` handling). With this change, `thor disqus import -c 'Some Category'` would now raise an unknown switch error, which is a concrete behavior break introduced by the diff. Additionally, the import behavior changes from creating a post with raw "[Permalink](...)" (and optional category assignment) via `PostCreator` to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which fetches and imports remote content instead; this is a verified, silent data-shape/behavior change in the task implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An already-shipped, unrelated migration (CreateTopTopics) is silently modified to add `force: true`, a change with no connection to the embed objective and no record of human acceptance. Anyone running db:migrate:redo (or re-running the migration against an environment where top_topics already holds computed ranking data) silently drops and recreates the table, destroying the data; the edit also buries an unrelated behavioral change inside a feature PR, so future archaeology of the migration history misattributes its purpose.

adjudication.rationale: The diff directly changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which can silently destroy any existing `top_topics` data if the migration is re-run against a DB that already has that table. This is an unrelated, behavior-changing modification embedded in an embed feature PR and introduces a concrete data-loss risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The already-applied MigrateWordCounts migration is reformatted (trailing whitespace stripped, final newline removed) as a no-functionality change bundled into the embed PR. The next change-safety loss is attribution: a functional edit to this migration later will be mixed with this cosmetic churn, and any diff-based audit of migration files now shows drift against the deployed version with no corresponding intent, making it harder to verify that production databases match the repository's migration lineage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a no-functional-change edit to an existing migration `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`: a trailing whitespace-only line is changed and the file now lacks a final newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). This is cosmetic churn bundled into an unrelated feature PR, and it can complicate future auditing/blame of migrations and comparing repo state to what was deployed, even though it doesn’t change runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The core revision path is changed from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, introducing a permanent validation-bypass lever into PostRevisor solely to serve the embed importer, with no explicit acceptance of that weakening of the shared validation system. Every future caller that passes skip_validations: true silently writes posts that skip all validations (length, banned words, topic state), and because the flag lives in a shared opts hash rather than a scoped importer path, the next feature that needs to 'skip one check' will reach for it, eroding validation guarantees invisibly — directly contradicting the PR's stated 'validation' objective.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new generic validation-bypass path in a shared component: `PostRevisor#update_post` changes from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and the new embed importer uses it (`TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). This is a real, diff-grounded architectural/safety concern (future callers could also pass `skip_validations: true` and silently skip all validations), but it’s not a directly verifiable defect since the bypass appears intentional for imports and the PR doesn’t show immediate broken behavior from it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new :raw_html cook_method returns the post's raw content verbatim (return raw), completely bypassing the sanitize/cooking pipeline, and TopicEmbed.import feeds third-party RSS/Atom content into posts with cook_method: raw_html, so untrusted HTML (script tags, event handlers, javascript: URLs) is stored and rendered unsanitized. Stored XSS on the Discourse origin: an attacker who controls feed content (any co-author on the configured feed, or a man-in-the-middle since PollFeed fetches over plain HTTP with open()) publishes an item whose content contains or

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new cook path where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using third-party `contents` from RSS/remote HTML (app/models/topic_embed.rb; app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so any untrusted HTML is stored/rendered as-is. The embed UI renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), making stored XSS feasible. Additionally, feed fetching uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (open-uri) and may be plain HTTP, increasing injection risk via MITM as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the raw URL into an HTML fragment with single-quoted attributes ("#{url}") and appends it to content that is then stored as raw HTML, without any escaping of the URL. A feed item (or embed URL) like http://eviltrout.com/x' onmouseover='alert(document.cookie) passes the /^https?\:\/\// check, breaks out of the href attribute, and is stored in the post; because cook_method is raw_html the payload is served verbatim to every reader of the topic and the embed view, yielding stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff shows `contents << ... I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}") ...` which interpolates the unescaped `url` into a single-quoted `href` attribute. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which would still allow payloads containing `'` and additional attributes. The created post is explicitly stored/rendered as raw HTML via `PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, and the embed view outputs `raw post.cooked`. This makes the injected HTML/JS persist and render for readers (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] PollFeed passes the admin-settable SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly into Kernel#open with no scheme validation, so file://, ftp://, or internal-network http URLs are fetched server-side and their contents are imported into public topics. An admin account compromise (or a site_settings write via any admin-reachable path) setting feed_polling_url to file:///etc/passwd or http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data causes local file or internal service contents to be parsed as a feed and published as posts readable by all users — server-side file disclosure / SSRF with no protocol allowlist.
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags PollFeed passing SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly to Kernel#open without scheme/URL validation, enabling SSRF and even local file access (e.g., file://) if an attacker can control that setting. This matches the golden issue of unvalidated open() on an attacker-controlled feed_polling_url allowing arbitrary URL fetches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The postMessage origin check uses a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of equality, so any origin whose string contains discourseUrl as a substring is accepted as a trusted sender. An attacker page hosted at e.g. https://forum.example.com.attacker.com (or attacker.com?x=https://forum.example.com-style substrings) passes the check and can postMessage {type:'discourse-resize', height:...} to resize the embedded comments iframe arbitrarily (UI defacement / clickjacking-layout manipulation inside the embedding page).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which only accepts messages when the *origin string* (`e.origin`, e.g. `https://forum.example.com`) is a substring of `discourseUrl`. The finding claims the opposite (that any origin containing `discourseUrl` as a substring is accepted, e.g. `https://forum.example.com.attacker.com`), but that would be rejected because `"https://forum.example.com".indexOf("https://forum.example.com.attacker.com") === -1`. So the described bypass/attack does not follow from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL", which is not a valid X-Frame-Options value; browsers that do not recognize it ignore the header entirely, so this response's framing protection depends entirely on the referer check. Any future code path that relaxes or removes the referer check (or a browser/configuration that drops Referer) leaves the embed endpoint frameable by every origin with no XFO backstop; the value should be an allow-from mechanism or header deletion, not a non-standard token.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the diff explicitly sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `ALLOWALL` is not a standard/recognized X-Frame-Options directive (common recognized values are `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and legacy `ALLOW-FROM`), so the finding’s claim that this value may be ignored by browsers is diff-grounded. However, this does not clearly introduce broken behavior or an exploitable vulnerability in the diff by itself because the controller also enforces a strict referer host check (`URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) before allowing the response to be framed; the concern about future relaxation is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The controller enqueues a retrieve_topic Sidekiq job for every request that misses the topic lookup, with no rate limit at the enqueue site; the 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever.retrieved_recently? keyed per-URL, so distinct URL paths each get a fresh throttle budget and the enqueue itself is unthrottled and unauthenticated. An unauthenticated client spamming /embed/best?embed_url=http://<embeddable_host>/<random> floods the Sidekiq queue with jobs (each job performs a Redis SETNX plus potentially an outbound HTTP fetch), exhausting background-job capacity; the per-URL Redis key provides no defense because the attacker varies the path.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` (no auth check, no rate limiting at enqueue time). The only throttling shown is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, keyed as `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (full URL string), so varying the URL path (`http://<embeddable_host>/<random>`) yields distinct Redis keys and bypasses the 60s throttle. Since `ensure_embeddable` only validates `request.referer` host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (a header clients can supply) and does not require a logged-in user, an attacker can flood Sidekiq with jobs that will at least do Redis work and may trigger outbound fetches via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`open(url)`), exhausting background capacity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url).read before any scheme/host validation — TopicEmbed.import's /^https?\:\/\// check runs only after the fetch — so callers that bypass TopicRetriever's host check fetch unvalidated URLs; the disqus.thor import path passes t[:link] straight from an attacker-supplied Disqus export XML into import_remote. An admin who imports a crafted Disqus export file causes the server to open file:// or internal-network URLs listed in it, with the fetched bytes rendered into public posts — a config/import-backed SSRF/LFI path distinct from the (host-checked) TopicRetriever path.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the diff shows `open(url).read` is executed immediately with no prior validation of scheme/host (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). The only URL validation (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) is in `TopicEmbed.import`, which runs after the fetch, so it does not prevent SSRF/LFI-style reads via `open`. The diff also changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` where `t[:link]` comes from the Disqus export, meaning a crafted import file could trigger fetching attacker-controlled/unsafe URLs. This is a verifiable security defect in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" never exercises the params.require(:embed_url) branch it claims to verify: with the default blank embeddable_host (config/site_settings.yml line 354: embeddable_host: ''), the ensure_embeddable before_filter raises Discourse::InvalidAccess before the controller action body runs, so get :best fails at the filter, not at the missing param. The missing-embed_url branch is asserted by nothing: if params.require(:embed_url) were deleted entirely (or if the filter order changed so the param check surfaced as a 500 instead of the promised 404), this test still passes because 'response.should_not be_success' is true for any error status — the spec name and the behavior it verifies are unrelated, giving false confidence that the embed_url contract is tested.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before the `best` action’s `params.require(:embed_url)`. `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), and the default in config/site_settings.yml is `embeddable_host: ''` (blank). In the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; response.should_not be_success; end`, no `embeddable_host` stub is set, so the request can fail in the before_filter rather than exercising the missing-param check. Also, the assertion only checks non-success, so it would still pass even if `params.require(:embed_url)` were removed. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test quality issue (misleading/insufficient test), not a direct functional defect in the application logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test that runs with the gating satisfied stubs poll_feed itself ('poller.expects(:poll_feed).once'), so the entire body of Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (SimpleRSS parsing, the url = i.id fallback for links not matching /^https?/, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and the TopicEmbed.import call) is never executed by any test in this diff. A regression in poll_feed — e.g. a feed item whose link is blank and whose item has no id attribute raising NoMethodError, or content mangled before import — ships green; the spec file exists but only verifies that the three SiteSetting guards short-circuit execute, so operators get silent feed-import failures with a passing suite.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the newly added `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` contains nontrivial logic (SimpleRSS parsing via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, per-item URL normalization with `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, HTML unescaping/scrubbing via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts guard conditions in `execute` and that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed` by stubbing/expecting `poll_feed` itself (`poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`), so it never exercises the body of `poll_feed`. No other new spec in the diff calls `poll_feed` directly either, so regressions inside `poll_feed` could pass the test suite unnoticed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both 'valid host' tests stub retrieved_recently? directly ('topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false)' / '.returns(true)'), so the redis throttle logic introduced in this diff ($redis.setnx on 'retrieved:<url>' plus $redis.expire(key, 60), lines 20-29 of lib/topic_retriever.rb) is never executed by any test. The real throttle code is only covered by mocks of itself: a regression where setnx succeeds but expire is never called (leaving a permanent key that throttles the URL forever after the first retrieval), or where the no_throttle branch (user.try(:staff?) from Jobs::RetrieveTopic) is inverted, passes the suite; only the one-line short-circuit 'perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)' is actually verified.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` directly (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`), so the actual redis-throttle implementation in lib/topic_retriever.rb (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` inside `retrieved_recently?`) is never executed by tests. As a result, regressions in the throttle logic (including forgetting to call `expire`) or the `no_throttle` branch (used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic when `user.try(:staff?)`) would not be caught. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" verifies only that the TopicView mock was constructed with specific args ('TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})') and never asserts anything about the rendered response body; the template then renders against a Mocha mock whose @topic_view.posts.present?, posts.each, and topic.url calls all return truthy mocks, so the 'success' assertion in the after block is satisfied by mock-driven garbage rendering. The test cannot distinguish a correctly rendered embed page from one that renders nothing meaningful: any regression in how @topic_view is consumed by app/views/embed/best.html.erb (e.g. best: 5 being ignored, posts not being passed through) passes as long as the constructor happens to be invoked with those arguments — the assertion verifies the mock call, not the behavior the test name promises.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example `"creates a topic view when a topic_id is found"` only asserts `TopicView.new` is invoked with `(123, nil, {best: 5})` and does not validate any observable behavior (e.g., assigns, rendered body, or that posts are used). Also, this controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so it cannot catch regressions in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` consumption of `@topic_view`. However, the finding’s claim that the template renders against a Mocha mock returning truthy values is not supported by the diff (no `render_views` and no return value configured).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update test asserts only 'post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/' and never asserts that embed.content_sha1 was updated to the new digest — the very field whose comparison gates the update branch in TopicEmbed.import (lines 30-34). If the update branch stops persisting the new digest (e.g. the 'embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)' line is dropped or writes the stale value), this test still passes because cooked matches the new content, while every subsequent feed poll re-enters the revise branch for the same content indefinitely — the test verifies the symptom (cooked text) but not the mechanism (digest persistence) it exists to cover.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`, the "Supports updating the post" example only asserts `post.cooked` includes the new contents and does not verify that `TopicEmbed#content_sha1` is updated. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, the update path is gated by `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and then persists via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. If that persistence were broken, the test would still pass while the system would repeatedly re-enter the revise branch on subsequent polls. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap, not a demonstrated defect in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The absolutize_urls coverage uses only 'http://eviltrout.com/123' (default port 80), so the non-default-port branch 'prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443' (topic_embed.rb lines 59-60) and the https path are never exercised by any assertion in the diff. A regression on that branch — e.g. unconditionally appending the port, or appending :443 to https URLs — passes the existing assertion, producing rewritten image/link srcs pointing at http://example.com:443/... in imported posts that no test catches.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls the prefix-building has a nontrivial branch to append ":#{uri.port}" when the port is neither 80 nor 443, and it depends on uri.scheme/host (topic_embed.rb). The added spec (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb) only exercises an http URL with the default port (http://eviltrout.com/123) and asserts rewritten links/images without any port, so the non-default-port branch and an https case are not covered by any assertion. This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly added URL-rewrite logic, not a demonstrated defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration defaults posts.cook_method to 1, which is :raw_html in Post.cook_methods (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns regular=0, raw_html=1), so every existing post and every newly created post without an explicit cook_method is silently reclassified as raw HTML. Post#cook returns `raw` whenever cook_method == raw_html (app/models/post.rb:131-133), so after this migration every pre-existing post renders its uncooked markdown source as its cooked HTML, and all new posts created via the normal PostCreator path (which never sets cook_method) inherit the DB default of 1 and are likewise rendered raw. The author's own spec (topic_embed_spec.rb) proves the value mapping: posts created with cook_method raw_html assert `post.cooked.should == post.raw`. This is a silent reclassification of the entire posts table on deploy; the correct default for the new column is 0 (:regular).

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on an assumed Enum mapping (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) => regular=0, raw_html=1). That mapping is not shown anywhere in the diff, so the claim that the DB default of 1 corresponds to :raw_html is not verifiable from the PR. In fact, the diff itself strongly suggests a 1-based enum convention: the code already uses Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action) for Post.types, and the new migration sets cook_method default: 1 (which would be an odd choice if 1 meant the *second* enum value). The added spec only asserts equality to Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] and that raw_html posts have cooked==raw; it does not prove raw_html maps to 1. Therefore the “silent reclassification of the entire posts table” conclusion is unsupported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This diff adds `force: true` to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making it destructive if it is ever re-run (db:migrate:redo, a restored/mis-recorded schema_migrations row, or an environment replaying the version). Any re-execution of this migration silently drops the existing top_topics table and all of its rows before recreating it empty, destroying the per-topic ranking data until the recalculation job rebuilds it; on a shipped migration this is pure risk with no benefit, since the table already exists in every deployed database. The force: true should be reverted on this already-applied migration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can destroy existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., redo, replay, inconsistent schema_migrations). This is a destructive behavior change introduced by the diff with clear data-loss risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_embeds stores topic_id and post_id with null: false but no foreign keys and the diff adds no cleanup hook for deleting the referenced topic or post, so rows are orphaned when a topic is destroyed. When a topic created by embedding is deleted (a normal moderator action), its topic_embeds row survives; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed then keeps returning the dead topic_id, so the embed widget resolves an embed for every page load and EmbedController builds a TopicView against a nonexistent topic instead of falling through to the retrieve/re-create path. A dependent cleanup (or an explicit delete in the topic-destruction path) is needed to keep the mapping table consistent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` declared `null: false` (migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`) and a lookup path that trusts this mapping (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` just plucks `topic_id`; `EmbedController#best` immediately does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` when a mapping exists). In the diff, there are no foreign keys, no `dependent: :destroy`, and no other shown cleanup on topic/post deletion, so a destroyed topic/post can leave behind a `topic_embeds` row that will keep returning a stale `topic_id` and prevent the controller from taking the “enqueue retrieve_topic + render loading” path. That’s a correctness issue introduced by the new mapping table + lookup logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote calls open(url).read with no explicit open/read timeout and no size cap, buffering the entire remote document in memory. An article served by a slow or broken host wedges the Sidekiq worker for the whole TCP/HTTP timeout window per attempt, and a large or deliberately endless response is read fully into memory; the embed page the user came from just keeps showing the loading screen with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the diff introduces `open(url).read` (in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) which reads the entire remote response into memory and provides no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or any response size cap. This can hang a Sidekiq job on slow/broken hosts and can exhaust memory on very large or unbounded responses. The same pattern also appears in `Jobs::PollFeed` via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. This is a real robustness/security defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no timeout and no cap on the downloaded feed size. A feed host that hangs or serves a huge body stalls the hourly scheduled job slot; with sidekiq_options retry: false the cycle simply does not run again until the next hour, during which no feed importing happens at all.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (via `open-uri`) with no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` and no limit on response size. This can hang a Sidekiq worker thread or consume excessive memory/bandwidth if the remote feed is slow or huge, breaking or delaying feed imports. The diff also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, increasing the impact if a run fails/hangs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rss.items.each loop has no per-item error isolation: an item lacking a `content` tag (e.g. RSS feeds with only <description>), lacking `id` when `link` is unusable, or whose link passes the /^https?\:\/\// regex but fails URI parsing in absolutize_urls raises and aborts the whole loop. One malformed feed item permanently halts import of every item after it: items before the failure are imported, the rest are silently skipped, and with retry: false nothing re-attempts until the next hourly run — the feed silently stops importing new posts while the job still 'ran'.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` without any per-item rescue. If `i.content` is `nil` (common when feeds only have `<description>`), `nil.scrub` will raise and abort the entire job mid-loop. Also, `TopicEmbed.import` calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` which does `URI(url)` and does not rescue `URI::InvalidURIError`; a malformed-but-regex-matching `url` would raise and similarly abort processing remaining items. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that failure will not be retried by Sidekiq and will prevent importing later items in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 60-second throttle key is written to redis (setnx + expire) inside retrieved_recently? before perform_retrieve runs, so the key is committed before the retrieval operation has succeeded. When perform_retrieve raises (network error, 404, readability failure), the key persists for 60 seconds so every subsequent retry job executes retrieve, hits retrieved_recently? and returns silently — retries no-op 'successfully' while no topic is created, and the failure is never surfaced to anyone.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieve` calls `perform_retrieve` only if `retrieved_recently?` is false. But `retrieved_recently?` writes the throttle key first (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` + `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`) and then returns `false` to allow `perform_retrieve` to run. If `perform_retrieve` (e.g., `fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `open(url).read` / Readability parsing) raises, nothing clears the key. Subsequent retries within 60s will hit `retrieved_recently?` (now true) and skip `perform_retrieve`, causing retry jobs to no-op without creating the topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loading page blindly reloads every 30 seconds with no failure state and no termination, while nothing in the retrieval pipeline ever records or reports that retrieval failed. If retrieval permanently fails (article 404s, host serves garbage, import raises), the embedding site's visitors see 'Loading Discussion...' refreshing forever with no error and no fallback link; the user-facing failure is completely invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` which unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds, with no stop condition or alternate UI. `EmbedController#best` renders this loading view whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, after enqueueing `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The retrieval path (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `Jobs::PollFeed`) contains no failure recording or rescue/reporting back to the embed endpoint; exceptions from `open(url)` / parsing or permanent failures (404/invalid content) would simply prevent creating a `TopicEmbed`, causing the embed endpoint to keep returning the loading page and the client to reload forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is dead code — nothing in this diff ever reads or writes the 'feed-modified:...' key it describes. Maintainers are misled into believing modified-since tracking exists; in reality the entire feed is re-fetched and every item re-hashed and re-compared hourly. Deleting the method (or implementing the conditional fetch it implies) removes the false impression.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Jobs::PollFeed` job (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`), the method `feed_key` computes a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` or reads/writes that key. The actual `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items, relying on `TopicEmbed.import` to hash/compare content, so the presence of `feed_key` implies conditional/modified-since tracking that is not implemented here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A retrieve_topic job is enqueued on every /embed/best request while the topic is missing, and the 60-second throttle is enforced only inside the job, not at enqueue time. Combined with the loading page's 30-second self-reload, a persistently failing retrieval generates a new Sidekiq job every 30 seconds per open embed indefinitely — unbounded queue growth with each job no-oping against the redis throttle.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view reloads the page every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so an open embed will repeatedly hit `/embed/best` and enqueue a new `retrieve_topic` job each time until the embed exists. The 60s throttle is only enforced inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb) which runs when the job executes, not before enqueueing, so you can accumulate many redundant Sidekiq jobs that immediately no-op under the Redis throttle, creating avoidable queue/worker pressure and potentially unbounded job volume if retrieval keeps failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update branch ignores revisor.revise!'s return value and unconditionally advances embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) even when the revision did not persist. If revise! returns false or its internal save fails without raising, the new sha1 is stored while the post content was never updated, so all future polls see a matching sha1 and the feed's changed content is permanently never applied — a lost update that looks successful.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` but ignores its return value and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly `return false if not should_revise?`) and its internal `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` returns false without raising on failure, this can persist the new SHA1 even if the post was not updated, causing future imports/polls to think content is up-to-date and skip applying changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import silently returns nil when post creation fails (post.blank? leaves no TopicEmbed and returns nil), and poll_feed discards the return value with no log and no error result. A feed item whose topic/post creation fails is dropped without a trace while the poll job completes 'successfully' — operators have no way to discover that imported articles are missing.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `PostCreator#create` returns nil/blank, the code simply skips `TopicEmbed.create!` and falls through to `post` being nil (`post = creator.create` then `if post.present? ... end`; method returns `post` at end). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each feed item calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` and ignores the return value, with no logging or error handling. This is a diff-grounded robustness/observability concern (silent drop on failure), but the diff does not prove that such failures will actually occur in normal operation, so it's not a verifiable defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) — a full remote feed fetch and import of every item — inline within the retrieve job whenever feed_polling_enabled? is set. A user's first embed view can block a Sidekiq worker on a complete, timeout-less feed download plus N import operations, compounding the missing-timeout exposure on the request-triggered path; a slow feed host delays every embed retrieval while polling is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve synchronously calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (no explicit timeout in the diff) and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item via `TopicEmbed.import`. This work runs inline within the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` execution path triggered by an embed request, potentially occupying a Sidekiq worker for the duration of a full feed fetch + N imports. That’s a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not a correctness defect per se.
